RFC 2545 Section 3: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." Tested: "only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." Gap: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if". Producer: internal/component/bgp/reactor/link_scope.go::thirdPartyLinkLocal, with internal/component/bgp/reactor/link_scope.go::linkLocalNextHop. The partial annotation remains accurate and owes the full include half where a third-party link-local is unavailable. linkLocalNextHop first requires one connected prefix containing both the recipient and effective global, then chooses the configured speaker link-local only for a speaker-owned global, or the neighbor-paired third-party link-local for another router. thirdPartyLinkLocal returns no address on absent, unresolved, missing-candidate, ambiguous or unreadable neighbor state, although the common-subnet condition has already held. refreshPeerLinkScopes and refreshForwardFactsIfLiveFrom refresh the scope/facts without re-advertising routes already sent. The default-originate and SendAnnounce positive/negative tests require the exact pair or global-only MP_REACH for the same configured speaker address and on-link/off-link recipient controls. TestRFC2545JointSubnetWriter and TestRFC2545ReceivedPairSubnetConditions inspect the complete emitted length/address/reserved/NLRI value and forbid withdrawal while varying same-link, split-link and off-link conditions; the functional joint-subnet carrier separately verifies distinct address ownership/topology and receiver subject/control bytes. The ordinary batch, queued-drain and named-commit tests assert complete wire delivery and accounting, while the policy-own-global test requires the effective post-policy speaker pair and unchanged legacy sibling through both forwarding rails, with exactly one policy invocation. The labeled-unicast static test and exact ExaBGP encoding pair supply their own on-link/off-link controls. The third-party announce/forward tests retain a valid neighbor pairing in their off-link negatives and require the third router's own link-local, never the speaker's, on the common-link positives. These assertions would fail if the tested scope guard were bypassed or required known-address controls were stripped. checkRFC2545NextHops still distinguishes the same on-link own-global pair from the off-link global alone on one session; checkRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocal still reads the sink identity, resolves its global/link-local pair and requires FRR to decode that pair. Both strengthened installation assertions now use native zebra JSON and require the exact selected, installed BGP prefix with the expected link-local active and in the FIB within that same route entry, using fields produced by FRR vty_show_ip_route and nexthop_json_helper. This adds installation discrimination without expanding Tested. The third-party interop checker actively resolves the neighbors and retries the announcement, so it does not test missing-neighbor discovery or automatic re-advertisement after a late entry. The declared Gap remains open; verdict remains partial with zero whole-requirement credit. This is source judgment only and claims no new runtime, mutant or revert observation.
